objective: Review the native Verilator option-parser boundary definition before allowing any non-executing dry-run check or parser implementation work.

review_decision.reason: The definition keeps the native boundary parser-only and no-execution, uses the expanded Verilator-facing spelling as the minimum, leaves wrapper/shim convenience behavior outside the native parser, and preserves coverage_output_equivalence as the later correctness policy.
review_decision.weakest_point: There is still no Verilator source tree or parser patch in this repository. Current support is wrapper/shim planning plus two static tracked filelist-template registry targets, so the next gate may only dry-run the handoff contract and must not claim native Verilator parser support.

required_handoff_fields_accepted: source files or explicit filelist inputs
coverage overlay or coverage top boundary
coverage manifest scope and compared output words
compare report path or deterministic naming rule

required_next_gate.name: run_verilator_native_option_parser_boundary_dry_run_gate
must_record: non-executing dry-run or preview commands only
the expanded future-Verilator spelling normalizes to shape 64x1 for the two static tracked filelist-derived targets
the synthesized command keeps ordinary Verilator build inputs visible and appends --sim-accel sidecar-gpu --sim-accel-states 64 --sim-accel-steps 1
the estimate command keeps --sim-accel-estimate-efficiency separate from the command-only preview
the handoff contract exposes mdir, top module, source boundary, state files, compare report path, and coverage_output_equivalence
invalid accelerator names, missing states/steps halves, non-positive counts, and mixed shape spellings are rejected by the shared compatibility mapper
resident modes and dataset-backed targets remain not-ready for the direct native-parser handoff
no generated report or artifact is treated as source of truth
no native Verilator parser support, arbitrary RTL support, dependency inference, automatic optimal GPU allocation, or timing claim is made

non_claims: not a native Verilator parser implementation
not parser inference of coverage manifests, host-probe metadata, source closure, state paths, or report paths
not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
not a runtime or ABI change
not a new public CLI or workflow
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
